overview.overview:
Indiana is projected to be one of the most Republican states in the country in 2028. It voted for Donald Trump by about 16 points in 2020 and by about 19 points in 2024, and its partisan baseline runs well to the right of the nation as a whole. The forecast gives Republicans a clear advantage, with a projected margin in the low-to-mid teens and a plausible range that still keeps the state firmly in the Republican column.

A modest national shift toward Democrats would narrow the gap somewhat but would not be enough to threaten a Republican win on current evidence. No state-level polls or home-state candidate information are available for this contest, so the outlook rests on past results and the broader national environment. Indiana is not expected to play any role in deciding the Electoral College.
overview.watch: A sustained, large shift in national opinion or a strong home-state candidate emerging on either side would be the most likely developments to alter the outlook here.
key_factors: Indiana voted Republican by wide margins in both 2020 and 2024, establishing a strong partisan baseline.
The state leans roughly 18 points more Republican than the national average, which is the largest single driver of the projection.
The national environment currently favors Democrats modestly, narrowing but not reversing the expected Republican advantage.
